name: Datadog
description: Let agents read your Datadog monitors and what triggered them, search events and logs, and query metrics. For first response to production alerts and incident summaries.
identity: A Datadog API key and an application key of a service account made for agents. The application key carries the service account's role, narrowed to the scopes you choose.

setup.title: Create a service account for agents
setup.body: Give the service account the Datadog Read Only Role, so nothing it holds can change your monitors or settings.
click: In Datadog, open Organization Settings, then under Accounts select Service Accounts > New Service Account.
Name: AI agents. Assign Roles: Datadog Read Only Role. Select Create Service Account.

setup.title: Create its application key
setup.body: Create the key on the service account and limit it to the scopes of what agents may read: monitors_read and events_read always, logs_read_data for logs and timeseries_query for metrics. Datadog shows the key only once.
click: On the Service Accounts page, select AI agents, then New Key. Name: AI agents. Select Create Key and copy it.
Edit the key's scopes and keep only monitors_read, events_read, logs_read_data and timeseries_query (the last two only if you allow them below).

setup.title: Create an API key and find your API address
setup.body: Datadog wants an API key beside the application key. The API address depends on your Datadog site: api.datadoghq.com for app.datadoghq.com, api.us3.datadoghq.com, api.us5.datadoghq.com, api.datadoghq.eu, api.ap1.datadoghq.com, and so on. You can test both keys with the command below: it counts your monitors and changes nothing.
click: Organization Settings > API Keys > New Key. Name: AI agents. Select Create API key and copy it.

Your site is in your browser's address bar while you are in Datadog. For app.datadoghq.com or app.datadoghq.eu the API address puts api in place of app; for a site such as us3.datadoghq.com it adds api. in front, as in api.us3.datadoghq.com.

fields.label: API address
fields.help: Your Datadog site's API address, such as api.datadoghq.com or api.datadoghq.eu.

capabilities.label: Read monitors and events
capabilities.description: Search monitors by status, tag or name, read one monitor with its query and the state of each group, and search events such as monitor alerts and deployments.
capabilities.note: Read-only. Reaches every monitor and event in your Datadog organization.

capabilities.label: Search logs
capabilities.description: Search logs by query and time, such as the errors of one service around an alert.
capabilities.note: Logs can hold customer data and secrets your applications wrote to them. Anything an agent reads may end up in what it writes.

capabilities.label: Query metrics
capabilities.description: Read a metric query's values over a time window, such as error rate or latency around an alert.

revoke: In Datadog, open Organization Settings > Service Accounts, select AI agents and revoke its application key, then delete the API key under API Keys. Agents lose access to Datadog at once.

tools.name: datadog_search_monitors
tools.description: Search monitors with Datadog's monitor search syntax, such as status:alert or tag:service:checkout. Pass page to read further pages, from 0.

query.description: The search, such as status:alert tag:env:prod

tools.name: datadog_get_monitor
tools.description: Read one monitor: its query, message, thresholds, tags and the state of each group, such as which hosts are alerting.

group_states.description: Which group states to include: all, or a comma-separated list of alert, warn and no data

tools.name: datadog_search_events
tools.description: Search events, such as monitor alerts, deployments and configuration changes, with Datadog's event search syntax. Pass next from the answer as cursor for the next page.

query.description: The search, such as source:deploy service:checkout
query.name: filter[query]

from.description: Start of the window, milliseconds since 1970
from.name: filter[from]

to.description: End of the window, milliseconds since 1970
to.name: filter[to]

cursor.description: The next value of the previous answer
cursor.name: page[cursor]

tools.name: datadog_search_logs
tools.description: Search logs with Datadog's log search syntax, such as service:checkout status:error. Pass next from the answer as cursor for the next page.

query.description: The search, such as service:checkout status:error
query.name: filter[query]

from.description: Start of the window, a time such as 2026-10-01T08:00:00Z
from.name: filter[from]

to.description: End of the window, a time such as 2026-10-01T09:00:00Z
to.name: filter[to]

cursor.description: The next value of the previous answer
cursor.name: page[cursor]

tools.name: datadog_query_metrics
tools.description: Read a metric query's points over a time window, such as avg:trace.http.request.errors{service:checkout}.as_count().

from.description: Start of the window, seconds since 1970

to.description: End of the window, seconds since 1970
